transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Hello, doctor. I keep holding on to this belief that my clients and managers are secretly monitoring and using my translations in ways they deny, and nothing anyone says can convince me otherwise. It has reached a point where I felt I needed to speak to someone about it.
Have you ever heard voices, or seen things that others couldn't see, during this time?

No, nothing like that at all. I haven't heard any voices or seen anything unusual. My mind and senses are perfectly clear, but I just know they are secretly tracking and analyzing my translations behind my back.
Do you find yourself having similar suspicions or feeling like you can't trust people in other areas of your life, such as your family, friends, or neighbors?

No, not at all, as I trust my family, friends, and neighbors completely. My concerns are strictly focused on my clients, my managers, and how they are secretly using my translations. While my wife and I argue about my work decisions—like why I turned down a promotion or avoid certain trips—I trust her 100% and don't suspect her or anyone else outside of work.
Have you noticed any difficulty keeping your thoughts organized, or has anyone mentioned that your speech has become hard to follow or jumbled?

No, I haven't had any issues keeping my thoughts organized at all. No one has ever mentioned that my speech is jumbled or hard to follow, either. I'm able to express myself clearly, just as I always have.
How long have you been experiencing these concerns about your clients and managers monitoring your translations?

This has been going on for about eleven months now. It all started right after a tense video call where my managers challenged my word choices on a translation, and I've been convinced of this monitoring ever since.
Apart from your concerns about work, have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy, or interest in your usual hobbies and daily routines?

No, my motivation, energy, and daily routines at home remain completely normal. I'm still working full-time, paying bills, and managing household responsibilities just fine. The only disruptions in my life are directly tied to avoiding their monitoring, like turning down that promotion or refusing certain travel plans.
During these past eleven months, have you had any periods where you felt extremely down and depressed, or conversely, unusually high and full of energy?
No, I haven't experienced any extreme mood swings like that. My mood has been relatively normal, and my only real stress or focus has been on the monitoring of my translations.
Have you started any new medications, or have you been using alcohol or recreational drugs around the time these concerns began?
No, I haven't started any new medications. I also don't use recreational drugs or drink alcohol.

Substance use and medical causes have also been ruled out. Therefore, we can confidently make a final diagnosis of F22.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a non-bizarre, circumscribed delusion of being monitored and having his translation work secretly used by his clients and managers, which has persisted for approximately 11 months. He does not exhibit any other characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia, such as auditory or visual hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms. His daily functioning and behavior are not markedly impaired except for direct actions taken to avoid the perceived monitoring (e.g., turning down promotions or travel). Furthermore, there is no history of mood episodes (depression or mania) during these symptoms, and substance use or medical conditions have been ruled out, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for Delusional Disorder (F22).
